The same harness on the middle tier: stronger on long work, but in public Terminal-Bench runs in Claude Code it cost more in total and took longer per trial than the best tier.
The strongest Claude tier; dearest per token, though in public Terminal-Bench runs in Claude Code it spent less in total and took less time per trial than the middle tier.
Same model and harness as the one shot with steering added mid-run; the extra protocol is one more way to fail, checked by the same cases.
Mid-turn steering over a standard protocol, but needs the ACP agent binary and Node 22, which the measuring machine lacks.
A full agent from another vendor for a consumer that holds only an OpenAI key; no turn-limit flag, the time cap bounds it.
Codex on the middle OpenAI tier; dearer per case than the fast tier.

opencode on DeepSeek's cheap model: lowest list price of the providers, untested as an agent here.
The selected arm with a published minimal-change rule set added to its instructions; its own benchmark (grade D) claims lower cost and time, and the extra text could also crowd out the task.
The selected arm with a published think-first, simplicity-first rule set added; no licence file, so its text stays outside the repository and is read by name; no public measurement.

The hub as its own harness: the outer loop is the hub's (pursue to a milestone as the goal condition, one worker per solution so the worker hierarchy is the solution hierarchy, build_out, keep_better, the verifier), around a small adopted tool loop (shell, file read and edit) in the style of mini-swe-agent. On the same model, independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 rows put that minimal loop level with Claude Code (three models, within 2.4 points), so the inner loop is not where the gain is. Not built: the hub has no tool loop, shell tool or history compaction yet, and off Claude Code a Claude model bills per token.

The hub's own loop speaking Anthropic tool use with the Claude Code tool names and shapes, so no calls are spent teaching a protocol and no Claude Code process is needed; the hub's frame, plan, ceilings and checks are kept. Costs per token on an API key (no subscription route), which is the one risk.
The same open-source loop inside the hub's shared wrapper: the frame as its instructions, shared ceilings, the code check with the stop decision, an outside-folder report. Per token on an API key.

The hub's frame on Claude Code's own loop, with the frame sized to the task and the after-check kept to what it can find. Written 2026-11-10 before its first run, from the totals of the framed arm (cheaper than plain Claude Code on the open-ended set, dearer on the hard set). Hypotheses stated before measuring: H1 the files in view (up to 60000 characters, carried on every turn) are the largest cost on the hard cases, so capping them to what the goal names and an outline lowers cost with no loss of passes; H2 a stable rules block ahead of the changing notes keeps the provider's prompt cache hitting across runs, so cache creation falls; H3 the resumed turn after the code check costs a full replay of the context, and resuming only for a named file that does not exist (never for a figure) removes most of it; H4 the plan-keeping rule adds turns on small tasks, so a task over a folder of few files skips it (decided by counts of files and characters, not words); H5 the judged deliverables fail for the framed arm because the frame tells the model not to read files in view again, so a cited note is quoted from memory; the winning bare opencode runs read their sources before writing. Status 2026-11-10: built and unit tested, not yet measured (no run was made), so it has no result and cannot be selected. Per-session data of the framed arm's hard runs already weaken H1 (frames were 1.7 to 5.8 thousand characters there). Kept only if the measured pass count is not lower and the cost or time per case is lower than plain Claude Code on repeated runs.
